title: Data Flow Layer Architecture (10-Stage Pipeline)
purpose: Document the cross-cutting 10-stage data lifecycle pipeline shared across all 14 features, with per-stage deviations and the caching gap
audience: Backend developers, architects, new engineers onboarding, platform maintainers
description: The data flow layer architecture defines a 10-stage pipeline that every feature's data traverses: Origin (where data enters — REST POST body, R2 upload via Multer, Socket.IO event, cron), Validation (Zod schema, manual checks, Multer MIME filter, Supabase Auth), Transformation (controller reshapes request, sharp/ffmpeg for media, fee calculation), Storage (Model.create() → INSERT, R2 s3.putObject, JSONB append), Caching (currently absent across all features — marked as gap), Retrieval (Model.findById() → response, signed URLs, aggregation queries), Modification (Model.update() → SET, JSONB append, R2 delete+re-upload), Deletion (Model.delete() → hard delete, R2 cleanup cascade), Synchronization (Ticket↔DM sync, notification after publish, payout after earnings aggregation — least standardized stage), and External Transmission (response JSON to client, Socket.IO broadcast, R2 upload, Stripe API, OpenAI API, Ethereum RPC). The complete absence of caching (Stage 5) is a cross-cutting concern.

nodes.label: Stage 1: Origin
nodes.description: Where data enters the system. Standard: REST POST body → controller. Deviations: R2 upload via Multer middleware (content creation), Socket.IO event (messaging), cron/internal triggers (scheduled tasks, background processing).

nodes.label: Stage 2: Validation
nodes.description: Input validation. Standard: Zod schema validation or manual field checks in controller. Deviations: Multer MIME type filter (content upload), Supabase Auth (login/registration), express-validator middleware.

nodes.label: Stage 3: Transformation
nodes.description: Data reshaping. Standard: Controller reshapes request body for service. Deviations: reshapeUserForApp (auth snake_case→camelCase), sharp thumbnail generation (images), ffmpeg screenshot (videos), fee calculation (payments 12.5% commission).

nodes.label: Stage 4: Storage
nodes.description: Persistence. Standard: Model.create() → SQL INSERT. Deviations: R2 s3.putObject (content files), JSONB append (support ticket conversation array), R2 upload (avatars/verification docs).

nodes.label: Stage 5: Caching [GAP]
nodes.description: CACHING IS ABSENT ACROSS ALL FEATURES. No Redis, memcached, or in-memory caching. Every request queries the database directly. Signed URLs (60s-3600s) are the closest thing to caching but are per-request generated.

nodes.label: Stage 6: Retrieval
nodes.description: Data reading. Standard: Model.findById() → JSON response. Deviations: Signed URL generation (content media), aggregation COUNT(*) queries (analytics, admin dashboard), enriched notification fetch (attaching creator/content data).

nodes.label: Stage 7: Modification
nodes.description: Data updates. Standard: Model.update() → SQL SET. Deviations: JSONB append (support ticket conversation), R2 delete + re-upload (content file replacement — though content files are immutable after creation).

nodes.label: Stage 8: Deletion
nodes.description: Data removal. Standard: Model.delete() → hard delete (DB row removed). Deviations: R2 cleanup cascade (content deletion removes associated R2 files), auth user + profile cleanup (signup orphan cleanup on failure). Most entities use soft-delete or status change.

nodes.label: Stage 9: Synchronization
nodes.description: Cross-feature data sync. Standard: none (most features don't sync). Deviations: Ticket↔DM sync (support ticket reply creates DM), notification after content publish (fire-and-forget subscriber notification), payout after earnings aggregation.

nodes.label: Stage 10: External Transmission
nodes.description: Data sent outside the system. Standard: Response JSON to HTTP client. Deviations: Socket.IO broadcast (real-time messaging), R2 upload (media storage), Stripe API (payment processing), OpenAI API (AI captions), Ethereum RPC (crypto payment verification), SMTP (email — unused).

nodes.label: Validation Failure Handling
nodes.description: If validation fails at Stage 2, appropriate HTTP error returned (400 Bad Request, 401 Unauthorized, 403 Forbidden) depending on the validation type

nodes.label: Storage Rollback on Failure
nodes.description: If any stage after storage fails, rollback mechanisms: content creation deletes previously uploaded R2 files, auth signup deletes orphan auth user if profile creation fails, R2 cleanup cascade on content deletion failure.

connections.label: No cache — pass through (always falls through)
Synced data ready for external transmission

errorPaths.destination: HTTP 400/401/403 error returned to client; pipeline stops
Rollback: delete previously uploaded files (content); delete orphan auth user (signup)
errorPaths.recovery: Error 500 returned; cleanup may have orphaned resources if rollback fails

errorPaths.destination: External API error; data may be persisted but not transmitted
errorPaths.recovery: Retry logic only exists for R2 upload (3 retries, exponential backoff); other external calls have no retry

errorPaths.destination: Primary operation succeeds but sync step fails silently (fire-and-forget pattern)
errorPaths.recovery: Synchronization is best-effort; errors logged but not retried

validationRules: All data must pass through Stage 2 (Validation) before reaching storage
Deviations from standard pipeline must be documented per feature
Stage 5 (Caching) is a known gap — no caching exists across any feature
Stage 9 (Synchronization) is the least standardized — only 3 features implement it
businessRules: Caching (Stage 5) is entirely absent — each request hits the database
Synchronization (Stage 9) is implemented by: support ticket↔DM sync, notification after publish, payout after earnings aggregation
Only R2 upload has retry logic (3 attempts, exponential backoff) — no other stage has retries
Only content creation has rollback (deletes R2 files if DB insert fails)
securityConsiderations: Validation at Stage 2 prevents injection and malformed data
No caching means no stale cache data exposure but also no cache poisoning surface
External transmission (Stage 10) sends data to third-party APIs — data classification should be checked before transmission
Synchronization (Stage 9) can create data consistency issues if not atomic
performanceConsiderations: No caching (Stage 5) means every request is a full database query — no read amplification reduction
Aggregation queries (Stage 6) run raw COUNT(*) without pre-computed summaries
Synchronization (Stage 9) adds latency to the request-response cycle for features that implement it
External transmission (Stage 10) can add 1-10 seconds depending on API latency (AI, Blockchain RPC)

annotations.label: 🟡 Stage 5: No Caching
annotations.description: Caching is entirely absent across all features. Every request queries the database. This is a cross-cutting performance concern.

annotations.label: 🟡 Stage 9: Least Standardized
annotations.description: Only 3 of 14 features implement synchronization: Ticket↔DM sync, notification after publish, payout after earnings aggregation.

annotations.label: Only rollback exists in content creation
annotations.description: If content DB insert fails after R2 upload, previously uploaded files are cleaned up.

annotations.label: Only R2 upload has retry logic
annotations.description: 3 attempts with exponential backoff (500ms, 1000ms, 2000ms). No other stage or external call has retry.
